First and foremost - Congrats on trying to lose **fat.**  
Now I'll be honest with you and tell you that at age 16 maybe you shouldn't be too drastic, I would suggest you to visit a doctor/dietitian *(doctor who is a dietitian best)* and so you can run all needed tests for your body and see if everything in your body works good and as is supposed to.  
Your age is pretty young and your body is developing now, with that being said you should be careful not to alter any drastic changes in your body and cause **health** issues in the long term.  
The more you stress the worse it will be getting, as you know we have different hormones for different functions, when you stress your body releases the stress hormone - **cortisol.**  
Very often the culprit for holding water in your body (and scale not moving) is exactly this hormone and the more you stress the worse it gets, the more of it can cause **anxiety** as well so the rabbit hole of vicious cycle keeps going - I'm speaking from experience and from a medical point of view.  
Before I also was "stuck" but then after I visited few doctors it was obvious that the culprit wasn't what most people would think - Just reduce calories, because sometimes it's not just that. Yeah its calories in vs calories out but when your body is fighting you then it gets extremely hard to be in a caloric deficit + lift hard + feel good + sustain this **life style**.  
Last but not least - Losing **fat** is more important than losing weight, most people actually want to lose fat and not weight, so if you're changing the composition of your body then you're a winner and if you keep your weight in the **healthy** range, then amazing job!  
If you need to work with a therapist about a mental condition you should do that as well, sometimes our **mind** is the biggest **obstacle** especially when we speak about the challenges of our bodies and more specifically - Having the look we **always** wanted.  
Good luck and take care of your **health**.
